continuity_scope: Original Studio Ghibli Japanese animated film, もののけ姫 / Princess Mononoke (1997), written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki; 133-minute Japanese theatrical work released by Toho on 12 July 1997. GKIDS's current English distributor page is used as a separate English-localization/release-profile witness, not as a replacement for the original Japanese film.
work_or_witnesses: もののけ姫 / Princess Mononoke, original Studio Ghibli animated film (1997)
GKIDS official Princess Mononoke distributor profile
Studio Ghibli production diary, used narrowly for Japanese cast-role naming
coverage_rule: Include the named individual dramatic characters directly named by the official distributor synopsis and supported by official Studio Ghibli profile/production material: Ashitaka, Lady Eboshi, and San (called Princess Mononoke in the English synopsis). Iron Town's people, wolves, forest spirits, animal gods, curses, industrial/ecological conflict, places, and broad communities remain terms rather than character nodes.
omissions: All further named film characters, individual gods/spirits, animals, Iron Town residents, clans/peoples, artifacts, detailed events, and ending outcomes are omitted because the narrow official release synopsis does not establish them claim by claim.

Manga, storyboards, books, merchandise, games, translations/dubs, and adaptations are separate witnesses; only Japanese-film production identity and English GKIDS localization/release metadata are used.

Environmental, industrial, Indigenous, leprosy, disability, war, and violence interpretations beyond the stated human/forest conflict and curse premise are not asserted as real-world equivalences or as established character attributes.
Graphic violence, gore, death, trauma, sexual content, and age-rating detail are not expanded from uninspected film footage.
uncertainties: The GKIDS synopsis names Princess Mononoke but not the personal name San; Studio Ghibli production material names the San role, so the alias join is limited to the same original film's official materials.
The official materials give no claim-level basis for detailed plot order, industrial technology, particular ethnic/Indigenous analogies, disease/disability readings, or the film's conclusion.
GKIDS lists Japanese and English viewing options and English voice talent; it does not establish that dubbed wording, performances, or name usage are identical to the original Japanese release.
The original-film scope does not establish continuity equivalence with storyboards, manga, books, games, merchandise, or other presentations.
evidence_basis: Studio Ghibli and GKIDS first-party release/profile material only; no fan wiki, Wikipedia, unofficial script, uninspected frame, or long dialogue reproduction is used.
